propositions: The completion verifier returns non-deterministic verdicts (PASS vs FAIL) for identical inputs within minutes with no code changes between runs, making the close gate unreliable in both directions: spuriously blocking complete tickets and spuriously passing incomplete ones.

The verifier's test-existence judgments are unstable due to variable free-form search strategies (literal substring vs semantic/regex queries with unpinned LLM sampling), causing false-negative criterion findings when searches happen to use semantic phrases instead of ticket IDs or exact symbols.

The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar lacks recorded verify_at_sha, trace_id, and input context, preventing stored data alone from proving input identity and distinguishing genuine non-determinism from input drift.

Pinning LLM sampling temperature to 0 (greedy decoding) by default in _verify_completion_inner reduces variance, and recording verified_at_sha and trace_id in the sidecar makes residual drift observable and diagnosable from persisted records.

The completion-verifier prompt and documentation do not clarify that search_files operates on literal case-sensitive substrings, leading the agent to issue regex/semantic queries that fail and incorrectly conclude test absence when literal ticket-ID or symbol searches would succeed.
